column2: Re-pushing to a tag that already exists in the repository — AWS rejects the push outright with a 'cannot be overwritten' error. A new build requires a new tag.

column1: Why does terraform destroy fail on an ECR repository that still contains images, by default?
column2: AWS won't let a non-empty repository be deleted unless explicitly told to. repository_force_delete = true overrides this, allowing destroy to remove the repository along with its images.

column1: What does a repository_lifecycle_policy actually do?
column2: Automatically expires (deletes) images once a repository holds more than the configured count — prevents storage costs and clutter from accumulating with no manual cleanup process.

column1: How is calling terraform-aws-modules/ecr/aws with for_each similar to Demo 17's security-group pattern?
column2: Both create multiple independent AWS resources from one module block, each addressed by its own key (module.ecr[\ui\"]
column4: etc.) — removing one instance's key only affects that one resource."

column1: Is a module's repository_url output just an inert ARN-like value, or something you actually use?
column2: A real, usable Docker registry endpoint — confirmed by actually running docker push/pull against it, not just reading it as a tracked value.

column1: What must every rule in an ECR lifecycle policy document include, or AWS rejects it at apply?
column2: An action block (e.g. { type = \expire\" }) — a rule with only a selection and no action fails
column3: since AWS doesn't know what to do once a rule matches."

column1: Why can a docker login succeed but a later docker push to ECR still fail with 'no basic auth credentials'?
column2: Docker credentials are scoped per registry hostname. If login and push target different hostnames (e.g. a hardcoded example account ID vs. the real one), the login's success says nothing about the push's registry.

column1: What three resources does one instance of this demo's for_each'd ECR module call actually create, confirmed via a real apply?
column2: aws_ecr_repository, aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy, and aws_ecr_repository_policy — a default, module-attached PrivateReadOnly access policy is created automatically even though this demo never asks for one explicitly.

column1: What real, transient error can occur pulling from public.ecr.aws, unrelated to any configuration mistake?
column2: toomanyrequests: Rate exceeded — the public gallery's anonymous-pull rate limit. Waiting a few seconds and retrying the identical pull resolves it.

column1: Why does this demo give each of the five services its own uniquely-named shell variable (REPO_UI, REPO_CATALOG, ...) instead of one shared variable name?
column2: Reusing one variable name across services risks a stale value from a previous service still being set when the next service's push runs — which can push the wrong image into the wrong repository with no error at all.
